content.value_statement: Teams can lose track of roadmap work when local plans and ClickUp tasks differ. This skill defines mapping, setup, sync, and conflict-resolution guidance for the official ClickUp MCP.
actual_capabilities: Maps local epics, milestones, and statuses to ClickUp tasks and subtasks.
Explains a local configuration layout for workspace, space, folder, and sync identifiers.
Lists setup, push, pull, sync, status, link, and unlink workflow commands.
Documents installation of the ClickUp MCP endpoint and OAuth authentication.
Defines conflict rules for statuses, points, and titles.
limitations: It provides guidance and does not implement a synchronization service.
It requires access to a ClickUp workspace and successful OAuth authentication.
It does not define custom field mapping or deletion behavior.
It cannot resolve conflicts outside the documented status, points, and title rules.

use_cases.title: Set up a roadmap connection
use_cases.description: Configure a ClickUp workspace, space, and epic folder before linking roadmap items.

use_cases.title: Prepare a safe project update
use_cases.description: Pull remote changes, review status, and plan a dry run before pushing roadmap updates.

use_cases.title: Resolve planning conflicts
use_cases.description: Apply the documented ownership rules when ClickUp and local roadmap values differ.

prompt_templates.title: Understand the mapping
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how local epics, milestones, and statuses map to ClickUp items.

prompt_templates.title: Plan MCP setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through connecting the official ClickUp MCP and completing OAuth authentication.

prompt_templates.title: Review before syncing
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a checklist to pull ClickUp changes, check sync status, and preview a roadmap update.

prompt_templates.title: Handle a conflict
prompt_templates.prompt: A local roadmap title conflicts with ClickUp, and the task status also differs. Explain which values should win and why.

output_examples.input: How does a milestone appear in ClickUp?
output_examples.output: A milestone maps to a subtask under its related Epic task in ClickUp.

output_examples.input: What should I do before pushing local changes?
output: Use a dry run to preview the update.

output_examples.input: Which title should win during a conflict?
output_examples.output: The local title wins because titles are treated as planning-owned values.

best_practices: Pull ClickUp changes before pushing local roadmap updates.
Use a dry run to inspect planned changes before a full sync.
Review sync status regularly and link items manually when needed.
anti_patterns: Do not push changes before checking for remote updates.
Do not assume unsupported fields follow the documented conflict rules.
Do not share OAuth credentials or workspace identifiers in public materials.

faq.question: What does this skill connect?
faq.answer: It guides synchronization between local roadmap items and ClickUp through the official ClickUp MCP.

faq.question: How are epics represented?
faq.answer: A local epic maps to a ClickUp task with the Epic type.

faq.question: How are milestones represented?
faq.answer: A local milestone maps to a subtask under its Epic.

faq.question: Do I need to authenticate?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented setup uses OAuth authentication after adding the ClickUp MCP.

faq.question: Should I pull or push first?
faq.answer: Pull first so you can review remote changes before updating ClickUp.

faq.question: How are title conflicts resolved?
faq.answer: The local roadmap title wins under the documented planning conflict rule.
